# ADR-1122: A pull request must kill every mutant in the functions it changes

## Status

accepted. Amends ADR-1115 ("No mutation run is part of the pipeline", owner rule 2026-10-22: mutation testing is scoped to the files a PR changes, never a whole tree). Uses ADR-0770 (`mutation_check.sh`) and ADR-0771 (registered equivalents).

## Context

Owner directive 2026-11-04: a created PR must pass the tests, the e2e tests and the mutation testing without a failure.

Measured on main on 2026-11-05: `scripts/mutation_check.sh` on one 365-line module (`mcp_server/core/ast_extractors.py`, four test files) takes 64 s and exits 1, because the module carries survivors older than any open PR (for example `_extract_python_func`, `_walk_for_calls`). A gate on the changed file would therefore fail every PR that touches it, for code the PR did not write.

Prior art: Google mutates only the lines a change touches and reports the result in review (Petrovic and Ivankovic, "State of Mutation Testing at Google", ICSE-SEIP 2018, doi 10.1145/3183519.3183521; Petrovic et al., "Practical Mutation Testing at Scale", arXiv 2102.11378).

## Decision

1. `scripts/ci_unit.sh` ends with `scripts/ci_mutation_diff.py`, so the `unit` job (and its coverage run) carries the mutation gate. `ci.json` keeps its five keys. Outside a pull request (`GITHUB_BASE_REF` empty) the step does nothing.
2. The script fetches the base branch, reads `git diff -U0 FETCH_HEAD...HEAD` (the merge base, so a base branch that moves on adds nothing) for `mcp_server/**/*.py`, and keeps the top-level functions and methods whose lines the PR changed, decorators and trailing blank lines included. A deletion of a whole top-level definition selects nothing; a deletion inside a function selects it. mutmut cannot mutate lines, so the granularity is the function, the finest unit it names. The deletion of a whole method selects nothing in its class, the deletion of a nested function selects its enclosing function. A changed function whose decorators mutmut 3.8.1 cannot mutate (anything but `staticmethod` and `classmethod`) produces no mutant at all, so it is reported as a `::warning::` and not gated.
3. Per changed file, the tests are the unit test files that import the module (`tests_py/scripts`, `integration`, `benchmarks` excluded). Imports are read with `ast`, so a parenthesized multiline import counts. A changed function whose module no test imports fails the job.
4. `mutation_check.sh` runs once per file with `MUTATION_ONLY_PREFIXES`; `mutation_equivalents.py` drops survivors and registry entries outside those prefixes. What remains is judged as before: every survivor is a registered equivalent (`memory/mutation-equivalents.json`, pinned to its diff) or the job fails. A mutant in scope that no test killed (`no tests`, `timeout`, `suspicious`, `not checked`, `segfault`) fails the job too, and mutmut runs with `--max-children 1` because the tests share one database that every test empties. The mutation sandbox copies `benchmarks` because unit tests import it. No wildcard, no per-file suppression.
5. Survivors in functions the PR did not change are not this PR's failure; a PR that rewrites such a function owns its mutants.

## Consequences

- Metric: surviving unregistered mutants in changed functions at merge: 0 (not measured today).
- Measured end to end on a real diff: touching `_callee_basename` passes in 44 s (its 5 survivors are registered equivalents); touching `_walk_for_calls` fails with 4 unregistered survivors.
- The `unit` job grows by about one minute per changed module. A PR that changes many modules lengthens it linearly; no cap is applied, so no change goes unchecked.
- Module-level code (constants, imports) is not mutated by mutmut and is not gated.
